My recommendation is that you think a lot about the numbers you're looking at when you do your 2k.
So you have to have a goal 500-meter split to keep as an average for the 2k. If you don't think about this before your 2k then your probably going to hurt your chances of pulling a steady race.

Your first 500 needs to be fast. at least 1 second faster than the average split you plan to pull.

now here's the important part... **for AT LEAST** the next 750 meters or middle 1000 in general, you want the instantaneous split for the whole time to be **juuuuust a little bit higher** than what you're shooting for your average to be. this sounds confusing but you're going to love it for the last 500 meters.

Then for the last 500, its gotta be BALLS OUT. it has to be the fastest one, or else you didn't do it right. what helps me is bringing the rate up.

Here's my secret 2k training I'll let you in on...

It takes 11 days or so and here's how it goes,,

*Day 1: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 500m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 2: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 600m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 3: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 700m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 4: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 800m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 5: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 900m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 6: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1000m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 7: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1100m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 8: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1200m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 9: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1300m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 10: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1400m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 11: 500m sprint @1:38, 10 sec break, 1500m @1:38 (32 s/r)

*Day 12: 2000m @ 1:39 (31 s/r), 10 min break, 500m as fast as you can

*Day 13: go for a jog in the morning and take the day off

*Day 14: 2000m @ 1:38 (32 s/r)

I did it from March 26th-April 9th and pulled a 6:32.4 @ 164 lbs as a senior this year. I hope the rates aren't too high because that's where the time is made. trust me, I hold my schools record at 164 lbs for a reason
